chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd al-Kirmānī, who said:

I ate in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام. When I had finished and the dining cloth was lifted, the servant went to gather what had fallen from the crumbs of food. So he said to him: Whatever was in the open area, leave it, even if it were a sheep’s thigh; and whatever was in the house, then seek it out and pick it up.

key_terms.الصَّحْرَاءِ: the open land or outdoor area
key_terms.الْخِوَانُ: the dining cloth or spread on which food is served
key_terms.فُتَاتِ: crumbs or small broken pieces of food
key_terms.وَ الْقُطْهُ: pick it up and gather it

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Muḥammad al-Jawād عليه السلام teach about picking up fallen food?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an etiquette taught by Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام regarding fallen food. It distinguishes between food dropped in an open area and food dropped inside the house, reflecting manners of eating, care for blessings, and practical conduct in different settings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4257 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Kirmani:

I ate in the presence of Abu Ja'far al-Thani Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad (as).
When I finished and the dining mat was lifted, a servant went to collect the crumbs of food that had fallen.
Imam (as) said to him: "Whatever is in the open area, leave it even if it is the leg of a sheep, and whatever is inside the house, collect it and pick it up."
